input.title: Proposal: budgets, merge approval, template weights, one log

input.text:
Four recommendations, each with its alternative in the file: /framework/ai/2026-09-30/servex-mastermind/merge-approval-proposal.md. Nothing is built.
1. Budgets: keep Budget: $N as the signal, add `foundational: true` on the assign line — then 100% is a report to you, never a stop; and a rule: reuse a live mastermind with the context before spawning a fresh one.
2. Merges: every merge becomes a row on its task card with the diff, the review and before/after shots at 400 and 1920. Foundational ones (full-size, or touching core/, framework.css, Servex/, Server/, ai/ code) wait for your Approve as an Inbox ask; light ones auto-merge. Reverse = `git revert -m 1` behind a Servex tool, logged on the same card.
3. Template weights: a library at /framework/ui/, one page per template with its weight and where it is used. Weight = who imports it (static, free) + a `use_template` tool backed by a node function that appends a use line to the template's own page.jsonl. Skill and hook can't record; the node function is the core, the tool its agent face.
4. One log, not two: keep page.jsonl as the only file; the line's key already says inbox / assign / landed / log; an interval job moves old `log` lines to page.log.jsonl (nothing deleted). Two files is your alternative; the cost is every writer choosing twice and every reader opening two.
Mark which ones to build.

Two more, from your last section (§5 and §6 in the same file).
5. The build loop: MVP → smoke + shots → quick layout check → an Inbox row mid-flight with the shots and one question (approve / recommend / improve) → your word → merge. The row exists only after smoke passes, so nothing broken reaches the site. You review on the main domain: the dev server serves each pool worktree read-only at monorepo.localhost/preview/qf-3/…, so nothing is merged just to be looked at. Done is a second line on the same row.
6. Path experts, what is missing for "start a mastermind in any directory": (1) plain minions and CLI sessions get no readme chain today (directory_of returns null — a one-line fix); (2) no directory has a standing mastermind — mint mastermind-<dir>, one per directory, dormant between prompts; its first turn is the read, questions fork it cached (experts.js), plans resume it; (3) nothing routes a prompt by path — the Dispatcher takes the path from your tab, a /path mention or the card and sends to that mastermind, spawning it if absent; (4) the expertise IS the readmes, and ext/Inbox has none yet. No new agent kind needed.
Mark what to build.

A plan for your new words is on this card (design-2.md). Any page gets a nine-grid shell: white paper in the middle and a gray well around it. A page's sidebars line up with its paper, and the ☰ drawer moves out to the window's edge, so it no longer cuts into AI 2's tab row. AI 2's right side will be the one chat widget from the dictation task (ux/Dictate/chat.js), not a new chat. I build it in three small merges once that widget lands.

Two more in the proposal file, from your last dictation. Graded rules: every rule on a design or code page starts with its grade — probably (the default; a reason in a comment is enough to break it), always / never (earned: a named breakage with a date and a link), and any grade can be broken in a rare case with the reason written where the break is; the review reads the grade, so a failing never blocks a merge and a failing probably asks for the reason. What stops custom CSS over the defaults (the sidebar not in Montserrat): the css skill re-prompts one graded line each time (probably write no CSS — the defaults cover fonts, colour, spacing, controls, text); review.mjs gets a defaults census that reads the diff — a font-family / colour / px-spacing declaration with no why: comment is a finding with file and line; and one review question measures the live font and colour by eval instead of eyes. The sidebar itself is a $3 fix on todo. design-code builds the graded list into /framework/code/css/.

The build has started, in two small steps, each with before and after screenshots of AI 2 at 400 and 1920. Step 1 is the nine-grid "paper" shell with one demo. Step 2 makes the ☰ drawer look like the site's other sidebar and hides the floating ☰ while the drawer is open. AI 2's own chat sidebar comes third, once the dictation task's chat widget lands.

§7, storage for messages, cards and threads. The rule in one line: everything is a page; it gets a directory when it has grown; until then it is a line in its parent's page.jsonl with an id, reached at parent/<id>/ by the parent's route(); a name that only groups pages (a tag, a kind, a day) is a namespace, not a page. Where per-path AI data lives today: a module's own facts in <module>/page.jsonl (a card is such a directory, so its messages are already lines in its own file); a task's record in ai/<date>/<slug>/task.jsonl; site-wide feeds one per kind in ai/ (log, day, board, cards, chat, asks, prompts, usage, verdicts, files); no ai/ subdirectory per module. Promotion: promote(parent, id) makes the directory with the line as its line 1, moves the thread in, and leaves a moved line in the parent so the old URL still routes; splitting off as a task is the same with the directory under ai/<date>/ and a from: field. Promote when a thread outgrows the parent's view, becomes a task or research, or you name it — never on length alone. ai-page documents this.

§8, the same widget with two ways to save, in Log.js's own idiom (plan only, foundational). Three additions: (1) an embedded item is one line, {"item":{id, parent, by, at, text}} — set() routes it to item(), the file stays flat and the tree is built on read, so a whole conversation nests without limit inside one page.jsonl; (2) a delta targets a deep item by path, {"at":"m-1/m-3f9k","set":{…}} — set() resolves the path through items and child pages and applies the rest to the target, append-only as everywhere; (3) promote(id) — a Server RPC / Servex tool moves the item and its descendants into <id>/page.jsonl and leaves {"file":"<id>/page.jsonl","moved":"<id>"} behind, so route() follows the old URL. One record interface {id, title, text, by, at, replies} is answered by both an embedded item and a promoted page, so chip, row, panel and the Reply button are written once. My promotion rule: first reply, or ~1,500 characters, or a title — never age. Optional hint: ▫ in the parent's file, ▪ its own page, on hover. Order when you mark it: item lines + Reply on every card first (that alone gives nested replies), then at-targeting, then promote, then the trigger and hint — each its own small merge.

§9, your chat-and-card model and the open question. Recommend: the session stays global and its focus is the selected card. One session follows you as today; every chat line gains a `card` field (what was selected when you said it), and the refiner writes item lines into that card's page.jsonl. So the card's file is the refined conversation, rendered the same in the sidebar and on the card, and the session's v-*.jsonl keeps the raw ramble with path and card on every line, so any stretch of it can be promoted into a card later. That split is by kind (raw vs refined), not by place, so no writer ever chooses twice. The mic row shows the selected card's name: switching cards switches the target, not the session; no card selected → the page is the target, as now. Alternative: a session per card, the card's page.jsonl as the whole session log. One file and no field, but selecting a card starts a different agent pair (context re-read, the reuse you asked for lost), the card fills with ramble the page view must hide, and one session no longer follows you. It fits one long deliberate session on a big card — which is what promoting that card to a task already gives.
